statement_short: Linear-probe transport: if the Euclidean two-point function of F has a positive spectral representation (mu >= 0) and obeys Bianchi including coincident points, then at the quadratic cumulant V(r) - V(r0) = -q^2 [a3(r) - a3(r0)] and the field of a static line is a gradient of a3, a3(r) = int dmu exp(-sqrt(s) r)/(4 pi r); hence a positive Stieltjes kernel on r > 0, which has the form of H3 with g_R^2 = mu({0}) when mu({0}) > 0, up to a contact polynomial; the gap is not implied.
assumptions: (E) positive Euclidean spectral representation of <FF>, assumed (E2b obtains its Minkowski form from W1-W3 and B for F, no W4, no CPT, through unchecked lemmas, and the continuation is unchecked); Bianchi on the T-product (equivalently, surface independence of the O(q^2) cumulant); int dmu/(1+s) < infinity; truncation at the quadratic cumulant; Coulomb phase mu({0}) > 0 for the profile
external_theorem_used: E2b Theorem (Kallen-Lehmann for a two-form field), resting on Bochner-Schwartz and the covariant disintegration over orbits; Wightman to Schwinger continuation; Fejer kernel; Tonelli
citation: E2b lemmas TO READ (Bochner-Schwartz; disintegration; continuation). Stochastic vacuum model for the D / D1 split and the area law, via Di Giacomo-Dosch-Shevchenko-Simonov 2002 (read: sections 2.1, 3.1, 3.2, 4.2); primaries unread
numerical_test: tests/test_e2c_transport.py (33 tests: sign anchor, component table, Stokes in momentum space and numerically, the printed boundary display, Fourier slice, T -> infinity with its q^2 C_eps/T coefficient at fixed regulator, the expansion of C_eps, flux profile, area slope and its 1/eps divergence; section 11: pair (anti)symmetry of the helicity structure in both signatures, its equal-time Bianchi violation without locality, the static-response identity)
unresolved_issue: Conditional on E2b's Kallen-Lehmann form, which rests on two unread lemmas; the T part of (E) then follows without locality, and the massless helicity term is excluded by (B_T), whose content on tau = 0 is two-point locality in that sector, so locality is assumed there rather than avoided (note section 11, argued with symbolic checks and independently re-derived; no source read). Says nothing beyond the quadratic cumulant (cubic cumulant zero only under charge conjugation; four-field cumulant, light-by-light in QED), nothing nonabelian, nothing about the existence of 4D QED as a Wightman theory. The general tempered case without int dmu/(1+s) < infinity, and the half-plane product delta(p0)/p1 for general mu, are not proved. The gap H2 is not implied. The 1/T rate is not uniform in the regulator.

statement_short: Static Wilson loop at O(q^4) in the one-loop Euler-Heisenberg EFT, for rigid spherical sources of radius R >> 1/m at r > 2R: the energy at fixed free charge is -c int|E_0|^4, c = e^4/(360 pi^2 m^4); the r-dependent part is a polarizability term -A/r^4, A = (5c/12 pi^2)(W1 q2^2 + W2 q1^2) > 0, plus a universal -c q1 q2 (q1^2 + q2^2)/(80 pi^3 r^5), with no r^-3 term and no r^-5 term from the q1^2 q2^2 sector; for (Ze, -e) the Z^3 part is +2 alpha (Z alpha)^3/(225 pi m^4 r^5). At finite probe charge Phi gains -8 alpha^3 q_W^2/(45 pi m^4 r^6), negative and gapless, so the limits q_W -> 0 and r -> infinity do not commute; the linear coefficient (Theorem A) is unaffected.
assumptions: one-loop Euler-Heisenberg EFT at first order in c and tree level; rigid, smooth, spherically symmetric, non-overlapping sources with 1/m << R and alpha q_W/(m R)^2 << 1; static, T -> infinity; charge-conjugation-invariant state for the absence of O(q^3)
external_theorem_used: Legendre transform at fixed free charge (div D = rho); Fourier transform of homogeneous distributions; multipole expansion
citation: Dunne, arXiv:hep-th/0406216, eq. (1.9) (read); Frolov, arXiv:1111.2303v5, eq. (13) (read; same EFT method, single-source limit)

unresolved_issue: Point probes (R -> 0) are outside the EFT: the coefficient of -A/r^4 there is set by the full light-by-light kernel and is not computed (magnitude, sign, finiteness). Derivative operators, two-loop terms and O(c^2) are only estimated. Says nothing nonabelian.
